 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Don't sleep on Week 8 just because there are only two games between ranked opponents on Saturday. A wild Week 7 showed us that this college football season can deliver upsets and drama at any moment.
 There's still plenty of potential for surprises and the action starts early with a Big Ten showdown between No. 6 Indiana and Michigan. The Wolverines' playoff hopes would effectively be kaput with a loss. Elsewhere, No. 18 LSU heads to the Plains to take on Auburn, which is riding high after its upset win over Georgia last week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The SEC has a pair of intriguing games in the afternoon window with Texas A&M facing No. 13 Alabama and No. 11 Tennessee taking on South Carolina. The Gamecocks are actually favored over the Vols.
 In the evening, No. 7 Ole Miss heads to Austin to meet No. 19 Texas in a game that feels like a must-win for Arch Manning, Steve Sarkisian and the Longhorns. Then the Big 12 takes center stage in the nightcap as No. 14 Houston takes on No. 10 Utah.
 Follow along below on Saturday for highlights, analysis and more:

 Sat, Oct 24, 2026 03:50 PM UTC Yahoo Sports Staff Week 8 viewer's guide
 After a wild Week 7, what does Saturday have in store for us?
 There may only be two ranked matchups, but there's plenty of potential for upsets. No. 11 Tennessee is an underdog on the road against unranked South Carolina. No. 16 USC is favored by just three points against the Badgers in Madison. And No. 19 Texas is in desperation mode at home against No. 7 Ole Miss.
 There are plenty of matchups that could go either way, so buckle up.
 Click here to read more from Nick Bromberg . 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 
 Sat, Oct 24, 2026 03:35 PM UTC Yahoo Sports Staff The SEC is a beautiful mess. Texas and Ole Miss are about to find out who can survive it
 Who's in line to head to Atlanta for the SEC championship? And as it turns out, this weekend might just be the first de facto play-in game.
 The Longhorns' comeback victory over then-No. 1 Ohio State is a long way back and growing smaller in the rear-view mirror every week. The put-up-or-shut-up moment for head coach Steve Sarkisian and would-be prince Arch Manning has arrived.
 Ole Miss is the more fascinating case here, because nobody's quite sure what to make of the Rebels. Are they the team that threw LSU out of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium back in September? Are they the team that somehow forgot that defense is part of the game in giving up 52 points to Florida just two weeks later? Or, like every other erratic SEC team, are they both?
 Click here to read more from Jay Busbee .

 We are somehow already halfway through the college football season after what was easily the wildest weekend of the year so far.
 What can we expect from the rest of the season? Our college football experts offer up their Heisman picks, title predictions, biggest surprises, disappointments and more.

 Sat, Oct 24, 2026 03:05 PM UTC Yahoo Sports Staff Best bets for Ole Miss-Texas, other big games on Saturday
 Money came in on Texas ahead of the Florida game, presumably because the Gators were going to be without starting QB Aaron Philo, but at this point, what quarterback would the Longhorns need to be playing for you to trust them as a favorite?
 Not Trinidad Chambliss, that's for sure.
 Ole Miss has regrouped in a big way after getting blown out by Florida, coming out of its bye with a re-commitment to defense, while also having arguably the best quarterback in the country.

 Sat, Oct 24, 2026 02:39 PM UTC Yahoo Sports Staff Steve Sarkisian: Arch Manning is 'edgy' after Texas' back-to-back losses
 Texas coach Steve Sarkisian says Arch Manning is on edge as the Longhorns head into the second half of the season without much margin for College Football Playoff error.
 No. 19 Texas is 4-2 after back-to-back losses to unranked opponents. The Longhorns were No. 1 when they lost 27-24 to Oklahoma in Week 6. And then they lost 27-24 to Florida as the No. 7 team in the country in Week 7.
 Click here to read more . 
 Click the photo to read the story. (David Buono/Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) 
 Sat, Oct 24, 2026 02:24 PM UTC Dan Wolken Notre Dame may benefit most from the 24-team CFP. How will Irish schedule now?
 Notre Dame has a choice: Does it want to do what's best for the sport, or does it want to create the easiest possible path to the playoff? 
 Because here's the difference between a playoff with 12 and 24 teams: Right now, Notre Dame is on the ropes because of its Charmin-quality schedule. After losing to BYU, the Irish have one more chance to get a great win (vs. Miami on Nov. 7) and one more chance to get a pretty good win (vs. SMU on Nov. 21). If Notre Dame doesn't beat the Hurricanes, it's hard to see how a 10-2 record of assorted flotsam and jetsam will be good enough to get in. It could very well be a repeat of last season where the Irish just miss the CFP. 
 Next year, though? All this hand-wringing would be a non-issue. Through sheer schedule manipulation, Notre Dame could ensure itself a bid every season barring some kind of injury meltdown.

 Sat, Oct 24, 2026 02:09 PM UTC Yahoo Sports Staff Oregon State's Jesse Legree staying in Corvallis another year
 Jesse Legree says he's staying at Oregon State in 2027.
 In a sign that the college football world is a lot different than it was just a few seasons ago, the star freshman wide receiver held a news conference Friday to say that he wouldn't be transferring to another school at the end of the season.
 Legree has 46 catches for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns through just seven games so far in 2026. He's the only wide receiver at the top level of college football who has topped the 1,000-yard mark this season.
